title: Weapons and Tactics Instructor (WTI) METOC (II/III) (LtCol to Capt) and (CWO5 to WO) NMOS (6802), DC I
raw_text:
2. MOS 6877, Weapons and Tactics Instructor (WTI) METOC (II/III) (LtCol to
Capt) and (CWO5 to WO) NMOS (6802), DC I

    a. Summary. Weapons and Tactics Instructors-Meteorological and
Oceanographic (METOC) Services Officers train personnel on environmental
characterization and effects in relation to aviation operations in support of
the MAGTF and aviation ground equipment, sensor, and weapon system
performance in relation to enemy threats. WTI-METOC Officers are proficient
in the development of environmental sensing plans to characterize the
physical environment and operational orders development required for
designated staff billets. This MOS is assigned only as an NMOS to qualified
METOC Officers and qualifies Chief Warrant Officers for the LDO program.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must hold MOS 6802.

        (2) Must hold the senior instructor (SI) designation per the MAWTS-1
Command, Control, and Communication (C3) Course Catalog.

        (3) Security requirement: must have a current single scope
background investigation/T5 investigation and adjudicated for sensitive
compartmented information (SCI) eligibility.

    c. Requirements. Must successfully complete the MAWTS-1 Weapons and
Tactics Instructor Course (M149721) Yuma, AZ.

       d.   Duties

        (1) Management of local or subordinate METOC technical training
programs.

        (2) Identify technical training shortfalls that prevent or hinder the
development of METOC products in support of decision makers.

        (3) Develop or assist in the development of technical training that
improves METOC support to decision makers.

        (4) Identify new or emerging METOC doctrinal support methods through
Marine Corps Lessons Learned.




                                         1-257                         Enclosure (1)
 1139                                                           NAVMC 1200.1L



        (5) Develop or assist in the development of new METOC Tactics,
Techniques & Procedures (TTPs) from Marine Corps Lessons Learned.

        (6) Develop the Annex H of a MAGTF or MSC operational order or plan
to support Marine Corps, Joint, or Coalition operations in support of
contingencies.

        (7) Develop MAGTF environmental collection plans that integrate with
Joint Coalition environmental sensing strategies to support Marine Corps
operations in support of contingencies.

        (8) Identify METOC sensitivities for MAGTF systems and operations to
establish METOC thresholds to support all elements of the MAGTF by
understanding the impact of the physical environment.

        (9) Identify METOC sensitivities for enemy systems and operations to
establish METOC thresholds to determine opportunities for exploitation of the
physical environment by friendly forces.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Teachers and Instructors, All Other 25-3099.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

 1140                                                           NAVMC 1200.1L

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
